summary: Emilio Teza was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Padua and under Anton Boller at the University of Vienna. He held professorships at the universities of Bologna (1860–1866), Pisa (1866–1889), and Padua (1889–1912).

Tibetology scholar Emily T. Yeh studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. Around 2003, she joined the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Somerville College and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She held professorial appointments at the University of Cambridge around 1988 and at Harvard University around 2008.

Emma J. Flatt is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She was an assistant professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (2012–2021) and became an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University in 2023.

Emma Salter works in religious studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Glamorgan, Cardiff University, and the University of Huddersfield. Her posts include tutoring at Greenhead College (2004–2007) and serving as Principal Examiner for the International Baccalaureate in 2019.

Emmanuel Forchhammer, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, studied at San Lazzaro degli Armeni and at the University of Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer. He served at the University of Rangoon and the Government of British Burma.
Emmanuel Lang was an Indology scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, where he studied under Sylvain Lévi.

Indologist Emmie te Nijenhuis completed her education at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning her PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Emmy Wellesz was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna between 1907 and 1921, supervised by Josef Strzygowski.

Enamul Haque, an Indologist and historian, studied at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991), president of the International Council of Museums (1983–1986), and professor at Independent University, Bangladesh.

Encho Tamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Kyushu University and Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Kumamoto University (~1962–1982) and Kyushu University (1968–1980), and was director of the Kyushu Historical Museum (~1984–1992).

Buddhist studies scholar Endo Asai studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as president of Minobusan University (1998–2002) and held faculty positions at Minobusan, Nihon Fukushi University, Rissho University Junior College, and Rissho University.

Eng Jin Ooi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from Universiti Sains Malaysia and Mahidol University. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Chulalongkorn University, a lecturer at Mahidol University, and became Lecturer and Dean at International Buddhist College in 2025.

Enga Teramoto was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He held academic posts as a professor at Otani University beginning in 1915 and as a lecturer at Kyoto University around 1928 to 1933.

Enichi Ocho was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa between 1926 and 1931. He was a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture in 1931 and later served at Otani University (1949–1976).

Enno Littmann worked in linguistics, history, and Iranian studies, studying at Berlin under August Dillmann, at Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Theodor Nöldeke. He held professorships at Strasbourg, Göttingen (1913–1917), Bonn (1918–1921), and Tübingen (1921–1951).

Enrico Pappacena was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Michele Kerbaker at the University of Naples Federico II from circa 1909 to 1914. He later served as a professor incaricato at the University of Bari from 1946 to 1960.

Enrique Soms y Castel��n was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Greek at the University of Salamanca (~1890–1913) and at the Complutense University of Madrid (1891–1913).

Enryo Inoue was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University in 1887, where he served as lecturer and manager until approximately 1905.

Ensho Kanakura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1926–1960) and Rissho University (~1957–1977), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education in 1967.
